svg.title: Plate PL-08 — The ratios: one plate, many scales
svg.desc: An engraved-style encyclopedia plate on allometry and dimensionless scaling, in seven panels. Panel I draws Kleiber's law as a log-log plot carrying BOTH disputed lines: a 3/4 line drawn tangent at about 4.2 kg and a 2/3 line drawn tangent at about 160 g, both tangent to the same convex quadratic of Kolokotrones et al. 2010, with the fitted data bracketed from 3.6 g to 460 kg and everything beyond hatched as extrapolation. The dispute between Rubner's 2/3 surface law and Kleiber's 3/4 from 13 points is labelled in a box on the plate. A residual strip beneath subtracts the curve, so that each straight line is seen to touch zero only at its own tangent mass and fall away on both sides; the cost of extrapolating the 3/4 line down to a 3 g shrew is measured there at 1.95 times. Panel II plots the local slope, a straight rising line, crossing 2/3 at 160 g and 3/4 at 4.2 kg: there is no single exponent, there is a curve. Panel III is a confidence-interval ruler of nine fitted exponents against the 2/3 and 3/4 thresholds, annotated that the nine rows are only five papers. Panel IV shows the claim dissolving on its own spread: 51 percent of compiled exponents fall outside 0.7 to 0.8, and the intraspecific mode is 0.667. Panel V draws the Strouhal 0.2 to 0.4 cruise band with the only per-taxon values this corpus carries, odontocetes and one bat, and prints the gap where the other named taxa would go. Panel VI draws the Froude gait transition at 0.5, the inverted-pendulum ceiling at 1, and the transition measured in actual lunar gravity at 1.39 plus or minus 0.45, whose lower bound never reaches 0.5. Panel VII carries the figure key, the numbered caption, and what the plate does not claim. Every line carries an evidence-class badge. The vertical datum of panel I is a stated drafting choice: no absolute metabolic rate and no prefactor is drawn or claimed.
svg.text: UNI ENCYCLOPEDIA & COOKBOOK · NATURA WING
PLATE PL-08
THE RATIOS — ONE PLATE, MANY SCALES
Source chapters: NA-05 (primary) · NA-06 · NA-07 · CN-08 · CN-10 · CN-11 · rows NA05-01…47, NA06-01…07, NA07-12/13, CN08-22/26, CN10-43/44, CN11-40…42 · corpus tip f1be794
~2 of 11+ developmental rungs earned
ZERO UNI CLAIMS ON THIS PLATE
A nature citation is never a UNI gate.
I
KLEIBER'S LAW — both lines drawn, and why they cannot both be right
Δ log₁₀ B (B in W · a ratio, dimensionless)
2/3 tangent
3/4 tangent
THE DISPUTE ‡
Rubner 1883: 2/3, from the surface law.
Kleiber 1932: 3/4, from n = 13 points.
Both are drawn TANGENT to the same curve.
Each is locally right, globally wrong. Fit a
mouse-heavy set → 2/3; a dog-and-up set → 3/4.
Neither of them is the curve.
the quadratic — Kolokotrones 2010 △ NA05-07
b = 3/4, tangent at ~4.2 kg ‡ NA05-01
b = 2/3, tangent at ~160 g ‡ NA05-02
×1.95 — a 3 g shrew
The 3/4 line, extrapolated 3.1 decades DOWN from its own tangent mass,
underpredicts the shrew by ~2× (0.291 in log₁₀) △ NA-05. Not catastrophic —
and THAT is why it is dangerous: a 2× error looks like measurement noise,
passes review, and is wrong for a structural reason no better data will fix.
1 kg
10 kg
100 kg
1 t
line − curve
RESIDUAL — the SAME two straight lines, with the curve subtracted.
Each touches zero ONLY at its own tangent mass, and falls away on BOTH sides.
body mass M [g] — log₁₀ scale, 7.65 decades
FITTED DATA — 3.6 g … 460 kg (local slope 0.57 → 0.87) · NA05-09
EXTRAPOLATED ◇
The residual strip carries the SAME curve and lines, with the curve subtracted. Its vertical scale is ×1.42 the panel above — the deviation is NOT
magnified; the TREND IS REMOVED, which is the only reason a 0.3-log error is visible at all against a 7.65-decade span. That is the honest reason
the dispute survived a century: on the panel above, the two lines and the curve are separated by ~5% of the plot height. The error hides in the ink.
Vertical datum is a DRAFTING CHOICE: b₀ is not printed in this corpus ◇, and a prefactor is unit-bookkeeping, not science (NA-05). Only SLOPES
and Δlog₁₀B are asserted. Curve from b₁ = 0.5371, b₂ = 0.0294 (T-corrected, M₀ = 1 g · NA05-07/08). b₂ is unit-invariant; b₁ ALONE is INADMISSIBLE ⊘
as “the exponent” — it is the local slope at M₀ = 1 g and moves if you measure mass in kg (NA05-08, MacKay 2011).
II
THE LOCAL SLOPE — there is no exponent
1 kg
10 kg
100 kg
1 t
2/3 — Rubner
3/4 — Kleiber
1 — isometry
body mass M [g] — log₁₀ scale
local slope d(log B)/d(log M) [—]
no-T fit
74 t ◇ EXTRAPOLATED
1.8 kg
slope(M) = b₁ + 2b₂·log₁₀M = 0.5371 + 0.0588·log₁₀M(g)
△ NA05-09 — linear in log M, so this panel is a straight line.
ONE curve crosses 2/3 at ~160 g and 3/4 at ~4.2 kg. The “dispute” is two
horizontal lines that the same rising slope passes through at different
masses. Kolokotrones et al. 2010: datasets with fewer large mammals give
smaller exponents — which IS the difference between White & Seymour's data
and Savage's binned data. Neither team was incompetent. Both were fitting
a line to a curve. ‡ NA05-07
The faint line is the SAME model without the temperature term: the crossings
move to ~93 g and ~1.8 kg (NA05-10/11). Even the mass at which “3/4 is true”
depends on which fit you took.
✗ Right of 460 kg is EXTRAPOLATION — rule 5's “#1 way scaling arguments
fail”. Kolokotrones et al. hedge the 74 t reading twice themselves: the rise
“may be due to the paucity of data for large animals”, and “If this is
correct”. It sits ~2.2 decades past the data.
III
THE VERDICT IS THE CI BOUND EXCLUDING THE THRESHOLD — NEVER THE POINT ESTIMATE (rule M2)
fitted exponent b [—]
Kleiber 1932 — the original
n = 13 points
interval NOT-READ ◇
no CI on record in this corpus
Savage 2004 — BINNED
n = 52 bins
includes 3/4 · excludes 2/3
Savage 2004 — UNBINNED (same paper)
n = 626 spp.
EXCLUDES 2/3 AND 3/4
White & Seymour 2003 — interspecific
n = 469 spp.
interval NOT-READ ◇
excludes 3/4 · includes 2/3
White & Seymour 2003 — interordinal
15 orders
interval NOT-READ ◇
excludes 3/4
W&S 2005 — true BMR (= row 4 re-rounded)
n = 469 spp.
excludes 3/4 · ~excludes 2/3
W&S 2005 — standard SMR
n = 469 spp.
includes 2/3 · excludes 3/4
W&S 2005 — thermoneutral RMR
rate REDEFINED
EXCLUDES BOTH
MacKay 2011 — 70 marsupials
3/4 nearly exact — for marsupials
Hou et al. 2010 — ant colonies
n = 12 colonies
0.81, 95% CI [0.55, 1.08] — off this scale in both directions. The interval excludes 2/3, 3/4 AND isometry alike: the study decides nothing. ✗ NA05-38
✗ COUNT THE PAPERS, NOT THE ROWS — the error this panel exists to expose, and which NA-05 caught in its own table.
These nine rows are FIVE papers. Rows 2–3 are ONE Savage fit, binned and unbinned — the binning is a defensible choice, and the choice is what produces the headline.
Rows 4 and 6 are the SAME n = 469 regression at two roundings: the 2005 figure is White & Seymour restating their own 2003 result in their own review. That is not replication.
Rows 7–8 change the RATE DEFINITION, not the dataset. Six rows of rounding-level agreement are not six independent corroborations.
◇ RETRIEVAL DISCLOSED: the Savage CIs are quoted from search-indexed full text; the PDF returned HTTP 403 and was NOT opened. They are load-bearing, so they are flagged, not laundered.
◇ The White & Seymour “±” bars are drawn as printed by the source. Whether they are SD, SEM or CI is not stated in this pass — so the bar is drawn, and the convention is fenced.
IV
AND THE “3/4 IS TYPICAL” CLAIM DISSOLVES ON ITS OWN SPREAD
Glazier 2005 — 146 allometric relations (Peters 1983)
range <0.5 to >1.0 · mean 0.738 ± 0.018 · 72% vertebrate, in a world where most animals are invertebrates ‡ NA05-45
Withers 1992 — 220 spp., INTRAspecific
range 0.3 – 1.8 · mean 0.724 · the MODE is 0.667, not 0.75 ‡ NA05-46
the “quarter-power” window 0.7 – 0.8
fitted exponent b [—]
fitted exponent b [—]
49% of Glazier's exponents fall inside 0.7 – 0.8. 51% FALL OUTSIDE IT.
49% inside
51% outside
✗ “Kleiber's law is a law.” — recorded NEGATIVE as a naming defect (NA-05). It is a robust
REGULARITY OVER A RANGE — a real and useful thing — and it is not a law.
✗ AND THE EXPONENT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE THE MECHANISMS
McMahon's elastic similarity (1973) and WBE's fractal network (1997) are incompatible
mechanisms that predict the SAME 3/4. Per M7, an exponent that multiple unrelated
mechanisms produce is weak evidence for any of them — and “the model predicts 3/4 and we
observe 3/4” is the most common malformed argument in this literature. △ NA05-36.
Elastic similarity then mostly FAILED its own test: Alexander et al. (1979) measured
mammal limb bones at length ∝ M^0.31, diameter ∝ M^0.35 — close to GEOMETRIC similarity,
not elastic (0.25 / 0.375). NA05-37 ◇ (primary paywalled; via secondary sources, which
give the species count as 37 against the 32 printed — the direction is corroborated).
And WBE's own finite-size form predicts CONCAVE curvature; the data are CONVEX. Not a
poor fit — the WRONG SIGN. △ NA05-18. What is refuted is the 1997 geometry, not network
explanations as a class. That distinction is the whole discipline.
V
STROUHAL St = f·A / U — convergence, and its scope
foil peak
0.2 < St < 0.4 AT CRUISE
Taylor, Nudds & Thomas 2003, Nature 425:707–711 · NA06-01
St = f·A/U [—] f in Hz, A peak-to-peak in m, U in m·s⁻¹
Odontocetes — SPECIES AVERAGES
6 spp. · Rohr & Fish 2004, J Exp Biol 207:1633
…but only 44% of 248 INDIVIDUAL values
captive · “considerable scatter”, their words
Bat — Glossophaga soricina, 4–6 m·s⁻¹
minimum-power speed · wind tunnel
‡ BELOW the 0.2 bound
Bat — same animal, 3.4–4 m·s⁻¹
Lindhe Norberg & Winter 2006, JEB 209:3887
Bat — same animal, below 3 m·s⁻¹
unsteady; lift/thrust production degrades
Eloy 2012 — the OPTIMUM is size-dependent
53 spp. · Lighthill elongated-body model · △ NA06-03
largest cetaceans → smallest tadpoles. Not one band.
SAME SYMBOL, DIFFERENT REGIME — do NOT transfer 0.2–0.4 outside cruise: water-walkers run
St = 0.01–0.1 (arthropods) and 0.1–1 (large) — Bush & Hu 2006, NA07-13. The scope IS the science.
‡ The band is a CENTRAL TENDENCY, not a law of individuals. Eloy notes the flapping-foil experiments
actually peaked at 0.25 < St < 0.35 — TIGHTER than the quoted band, marked here by the two fine inner
rules. ✗ Convergence across independent lineages is evidence of a CONSTRAINT-OPTIMUM and a hypothesis
generator — never proof that any animal's St is an adaptation (Gould & Lewontin 1979).
VI
FROUDE Fr = v²/(g·L) — the gait transition
Froude number Fr = v²/(g·L) [—] L = hip height [m]
walk → run, bipeds, EARTH 1 g
Fr = 1
inverted-pendulum ceiling △
MEASURED IN ACTUAL LUNAR GRAVITY
n = 8 · 6 of 8 chose Fr > 1.0 · De Witt 2014 — NA06-05
the lunar band's LOWER bound
never reaches 0.5
✗ NEGATIVE — Fr ≈ 0.5 IS NOT A UNIVERSAL GAIT CONSTANT.
It held on Earth and it FAILED off-Earth. A dimensionless ratio produced a real,
checkable prediction; the prediction was checked in actual lunar gravity; it lost.
The loss is drawn, not buried. Fr ≈ 0.5 is scoped to bipeds at 1 g.
Alexander; Kram, Domingo & Ferris 1997, J Exp Biol 200(4):821–826 — bipeds
“…all choose to switch … at approximately the same Froude number (0.5)”.
v = √(Fr·g·L) — computed, NOT observed △ CN11-41/42
We switch at 2.1 m·s⁻¹, well below the 3.0 m·s⁻¹ we could still walk at. The
transition is an ENERGETIC CHOICE, not a mechanical limit.
◇ A MEASURED absolute preferred transition speed, with its n, is NOT-SOURCED in
this pass (Kram et al. paywalled). Only the DIMENSIONLESS number is sourced.
✗ CONVENTION TRAP (CN-08): Fr = v²/(gL) and Fr = v/√(gL) differ BY A SQUARE.
“Fr = 0.5” in one is “Fr ≈ 0.71” in the other — the ghost tick above. A gait
threshold quoted without its convention is not a threshold.
‡ CLASS CONFLICT in this corpus's own ledger: CN11-40 classes Fr ≈ 0.5
OBSERVED-REPLICATED, NA06-04 classes it OBSERVED-CONTESTED. The stricter
class is carried here. See caption 7 — it is a choice, not a finding.
VII
KEY, CAPTION, AND WHAT THIS PLATE DOES NOT CLAIM
FIGURE KEY — marks, not colours (this plate must survive greyscale)
OBSERVED-REPLICATED
measured, and independently replicated across labs, datasets or taxa. Drawn as a SOLID rule or bar.
OBSERVED-CONTESTED
measured, but the community genuinely disputes it. Both positions carried; the dispute named.
OBSERVED-SINGLE
measured once; no independent replication on record. One study is not a literature.
MODELED
derived from a model that fits data. THE ASSUMPTIONS ARE THE FENCE.
NOT-SOURCED
a value this corpus could not trace to a source. A gap in our homework, NOT in the literature.
INADMISSIBLE
cannot be asserted as stated — unfalsifiable, or an artifact of its own units.
NEGATIVE / trap
a conflation, a defect or a failed prediction, recorded first-class — never deleted, never mocked.
Classes are NATURA classes (NA-00, amended 2026-07-15: twelve classes in three groups — measured / derived / fenced); this plate uses six of the twelve, plus the
first-class NEGATIVE record. They are SOVEREIGN from the UNI fence (proven · designed · hypothesized · not-yet-built) and never merge. Line weight, hatch density
and dash pattern carry every distinction colour carries.
CAPTION
1 · Panel I is drawn from THREE sourced constants and nothing else: b₁ = 0.5371, b₂ = 0.0294 (Kolokotrones et al. 2010, Nature 464:753–756, temperature-corrected fit,
n = 636 mammals, mass in g, B in W · NA05-07/08) and the local-slope identity slope = b₁ + 2b₂·log₁₀M (NA05-09). The 3/4 line is drawn TANGENT to that curve at
~4.2 kg and the 2/3 line TANGENT at ~160 g, because those are the masses at which each exponent is locally true (NA05-10/11). The vertical datum is the 4.2 kg
tangent point: b₀ is not printed in this corpus ◇, so no absolute metabolic rate is drawn or claimed. Reproduced here and checked against NA-05's own printed
arithmetic (0.263 − 2.332 = −2.069; 0.75 × (0.477 − 3.623) = −2.360; difference 0.291 in log₁₀ → ×1.95). If that arithmetic is wrong, this panel is wrong.
2 · The dispute is the flagship and it is LIVE. Rubner (1883) argues 2/3 from the surface law — heat leaves through a surface ∝ L², mass grows ∝ L³ — and that is
dimensional analysis, which is usually right. Kleiber (1932, Hilgardia 6:315–353) reports ~3/4 from 13 data points. Kolokotrones et al. (2010) answer that the
log–log relation is CONVEX and therefore not a power law at all (b₂ = 0.0322 ± 0.0053, P = 9.0 × 10⁻¹⁰). MacKay (2011, J Theor Biol 280:194–196) disputes THAT:
b₁ is an artifact of choosing M₀ = 1 g; the quadratic buys R² only 0.958 → 0.961; Hayssen & Lacy (1985) fitted and rejected the same model 25 years earlier; and
Order by Order only the Rodentia retain significant curvature — though MacKay concedes in the same paragraph that pooled across all eutheria it “remains
significant” under his own test. Deeds, Savage & Fontana (2011, J Theor Biol 280:197–198) reply — but they are THREE OF KOLOKOTRONES ET AL.'S OWN FOUR
AUTHORS, so a rebuttal by the accused, not an independent corroboration — conceding the b₁ artifact while arguing only b₂ carries the curvature claim, and
leaving MacKay's Hayssen & Lacy receipt and his 70-marsupial fit (k = 0.75 ± 0.01, R² = 0.990 · NA05-14) unanswered. The claim, the resolution, AND the objection
to the resolution are all contested. All three are on this plate, including the half that does not suit the fence.
3 · Panel III is rule M2 rendered: the verdict is the CI bound that excludes the threshold, never the point estimate. Savage's 0.712 and 0.737 LOOK like agreement;
their intervals reach opposite verdicts. The panel deliberately shows nine rows that are FIVE papers, because reading rounding-level agreement as independent
corroboration is the exact error NA-05 caught in its own table — and then had to re-class its own row for committing.
4 · Panel V draws only what is sourced. Taylor, Nudds & Thomas (2003) NAME dolphins, sharks, bony fish, birds, bats and insects as converging on 0.2 < St < 0.4 at
cruise, and this corpus carries per-taxon values for only TWO of them: odontocetes (Rohr & Fish 2004 · NA06-02) and one bat (Lindhe Norberg & Winter 2006 ·
CN10-44). Per-taxon values for birds, sharks, bony fish and insects are NOT-SOURCED in this pass ◇, so this plate plots NONE and prints the gap instead of dots.
Falsifier: read Taylor et al.'s figure 1 and print the per-taxon values it carries.
5 · Panel VI's Fr = 0.5 and Fr = 1.39 ± 0.45 sit on ONE dimensionless axis because that is the whole claim — a dimensionless number is the only thing that can travel
between a laboratory on Earth and a body in lunar gravity. The lunar band [0.94, 1.84] does not reach 0.5 at its lower bound. The prediction did not merely widen;
it lost. Lunar g is NOT printed here: only the dimensionless result is sourced, and converting it to a speed would need a gravity this plate did not source ◇.
6 · ✗ A SECOND APPLICATION OF THE SAME NUMBER ALSO BROKE, and is recorded here rather than omitted for tidiness. Alexander's trackway formula
u = 0.25·g^0.5·λ^1.67·h^(−1.17) reads a dinosaur's speed off a fossil trackway (1.0–3.6 m·s⁻¹ ‡ NA07-16). Prescott, Griffin, Demuth et al. (2025, Biol Lett
21:20250191) walked guineafowl across mud and found calculated speed ran 1.17× to 4.74× measured, typically ~2× ⊙ (n = 2, one species · CN08-26): “speed estimates from trackways are
inaccurate, if not outright misleading.” It is not drawn as a panel because this plate's subject is the GAIT TRANSITION; it is printed because a negative that is
merely off-topic is still a negative.
7 · ✗ TWO DEFECTS THIS PLATE FOUND IN THE CORPUS'S OWN LEDGER, recorded first-class and NOT silently harmonised. (a) Fr at walk→run ≈ 0.5 carries TWO
CLASSES: CN11-40 classes it OBSERVED-REPLICATED, NA06-04 classes the same quantity OBSERVED-CONTESTED — and the two rows cite DIFFERENT Alexander
papers (1984, Int J Robot Res 3(2):49–59 vs 1983, J. Zool.). (b) The Prescott et al. 2025 guineafowl ratio carries two classes: NA06-07 says OBSERVED-REPLICATED,
CN08-26 says OBSERVED-SINGLE (n = 2, one species). NA-05's own rule is that ONE RESULT CANNOT HOLD TWO CLASSES — it re-classed NA05-06 for precisely this.
This plate carries the STRICTER class in both cases (OBSERVED-CONTESTED ‡; OBSERVED-SINGLE ⊙) and prints the conflict. Falsifier: reconcile the four rows in
encyclopedia/NATURE-LEDGER.md — in each pair, one row must move. Until then the badge on this plate is the conservative one, and it is a choice, not a finding.
WHAT THIS PLATE DOES NOT CLAIM
· Not claimed: that metabolic rate scales as M^(3/4). Nor as M^(2/3). Both lines are drawn because both are claimed in the literature; the plate asserts NEITHER. NA-05's
position is that the question is malformed as usually asked, because the log–log relation carries curvature — and that THAT position is contested too.
· Not claimed: any absolute metabolic rate, or any prefactor. The vertical axis in I is a difference of logarithms with its datum stated. b₀ is not printed in this corpus, and a
prefactor moves by 1000^b when you change grams to kilograms while the exponent does not move at all. The exponent is the candidate science; the prefactor is bookkeeping.
· Not claimed: that b₁ = 0.5371 is “the metabolic exponent”. It is the local slope at M₀ = 1 g and changes value if you measure mass in kilograms (b₁′ = b₁ − 2b₂ log k).
Only b₂ and the local slope at a NAMED mass survive a change of unit. Quoted as “the exponent” it is INADMISSIBLE ⊘ (NA05-08).
· Not claimed: that Kolokotrones et al. (2010) settled the dispute, or that the curvature is a law of size rather than a between-Order artifact. That is exactly what is contested.
· Not claimed: anything to the right of the fitted-data bracket. The 74 t reading is an EXTRAPOLATION ~2.2 decades past the data, hedged twice by its own authors, and is
drawn dashed and hatched for that reason. A power law fitted in one range does not extrapolate through a regime change, and the fit will not warn you.
· Not claimed: that St = 0.2–0.4 is a law, that it applies off cruise, or that any animal's St is an adaptation. It is a central tendency at cruise; individual scatter is large
(only 44% of 248 odontocete values fall in 0.225–0.275); the modelled optimum is size-dependent (0.15 → 0.8); and one bat's efficient cruise sits BELOW the 0.2 bound.
· Not claimed: per-taxon Strouhal values for birds, sharks, bony fish or insects. This corpus does not carry them. The plate prints the gap ◇ rather than inventing points.
· Not claimed: that Fr ≈ 0.5 is a universal gait-transition constant, or a mechanical limit. It is scoped to bipeds at 1 g; the mechanical ceiling is Fr = 1; and the measured
lunar transition was 1.39 ± 0.45. Nor is a measured absolute transition speed claimed — the 2.1 m·s⁻¹ is computed from Fr and L, not observed ◇.
· Not claimed: that any exponent, band or threshold here is an OPTIMUM. Per Gould & Lewontin (1979), drift, phylogenetic inertia, developmental constraint, pleiotropy and
frozen accidents produce values that optimise nothing — and an exponent is an unusually easy thing to find a story for after the fact. Every number here is a hypothesis
generator. Per M7, a design taken from this plate must still beat a TUNED baseline on a PRE-REGISTERED metric with a discriminator that collapses the gain, or it is NEGATIVE.
· Not claimed: that anything here raises any UNI rung. A NATURE CITATION IS NEVER A UNI GATE. This plate contains ZERO UNI claims, and the honest program position is
unchanged by it: ~2 of 11+ developmental rungs earned, a developmental active-inference simulation. “Full human” and “beyond human” appear nowhere as targets —
they are permanent open questions, and reading one into a scaling law would be the exact lane-crossing this wing exists to prevent.
